Hi Sam — thanks for the checklist. Looping in Karthik and Irene for the technical and ops details.

Quick answers up front: we can provide the nodeclass matrix and a one-page MAP tomorrow. Below is a proposed starting profile based on what we discussed; Karthik will refine counts after a short workload questionnaire.

Proposed nodeclass profile (initial):
- control-plane: 3 x c6.large (non-GPU) for k8s control and controlplane services
- gpu-inference: 6 x a40-equivalent (NVMe local for KV cache; 384GB RAM) — sized for steady-state 250 rps inference with burst to 500
- cpu-batch: 4 x c3-highmem (32 vCPU / 256GB) for large batch compilation/quantization jobs
- storage-backend nodes (optional warm): 2 x i3/ssd-heavy for blockstore attach and snapshotting

Storage recommendations:
- Model artifacts: blockstore (iSCSI/NFS) mounted with provisioned IO — start with 10TB replicated across primary cluster fabric, snapshot daily.
- KV / cache: use local NVMe on GPU nodes; persist checkpoints to blockstore.
- Ephemeral scratch: node-local and cleared on job completion.

Attachments: RNF-nodeclass-bom-v1.xlsx (node specs + rough pricing) and proposal-stonebridge-v1.3.pdf (statement of work + timelines).

Karthik / Irene — can you confirm the GPU sizing suggestion above and whether we should recommend reserved capacity for the first 6 months to guarantee latency during onboarding?

Sam — once we align on counts I'll drop a MAP with dates that Procurement can sign off and include DocuSign.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Lead, Redwood Inference

Marissa — quick technical notes based on Sam's checklist and the proposed profile. Quoted below for context.

> Proposed nodeclass profile (initial):
> - control-plane: 3 x c6.large (non-GPU) for k8s control and controlplane services
> - gpu-inference: 6 x a40-equivalent (NVMe local for KV cache; 384GB RAM) — sized for steady-state 250 rps inference with burst to 500
> - cpu-batch: 4 x c3-highmem (32 vCPU / 256GB) for large batch compilation/quantization jobs
> - storage-backend nodes (optional warm): 2 x i3/ssd-heavy for blockstore attach and snapshotting

My take / clarifications:
- GPU count: if Stonebridge will run concurrent model families we should recommend 8 GPU nodes (not 6) to provide headroom for model rollouts + a canary pool. 6 works for single-model steady-state but tight for parallel experiments.
- NVMe sizing: recommend 1.6TB NVMe per GPU node for KV/cache (this keeps local cache TTLs reasonable). If customers want longer-lived caches, increase to 3.2TB.
- Network: 25Gbps per GPU node (minimum) to handle model artifact fetch and KV replication during warmups. Ask facilities for jumbo frame enablement on the cluster VLAN.
- Blockstore: prefer iSCSI-backed LUNs with multipath for model artifacts — 10TB initial, expand in increments of 5TB. Snapshot cadence: daily incremental + weekly full; retention business decision.
- Attach sequence:
  1) Ensure LUNs provisioned and mounted on storage-backend nodes
  2) Redwood operator runs attach job targeting storage backend and updates PV StorageClass mapping
  3) Warm nodes pull model artifacts into local NVMe caches (background)
  4) Route traffic to GPU pool after KV priming completes (health checks pass)

Operational asks for procurement package: expected lead time for A40-class cards is 6–9 weeks; NVMe+server lead times 4–6 weeks. If procurement needs SLA-backed capacity we should discuss reserved capacity clause in the SOW.

Irene — can you draft a one-page runbook for attach order and health checks? I'll propose node counts 8 (GPU), 4 (batch), 3 control, 2 storage-backend unless we hear otherwise from Sam.

Thanks,
Karthik
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

- Node counts: control-plane 3, gpu-inference 8 (A40-class), cpu-batch 4, storage-backend 2
- Storage: 10TB initial blockstore (iSCSI LUNs), snapshot policy daily incremental / weekly full; expand in 5TB increments
- Networking: 25Gbps min per GPU node; jumbo frames recommended; cluster VLAN and cross-connect details in attached site checklist
- Lead times: GPU servers 6–9 weeks, NVMe-equipped nodes 4–6 weeks, cross-connect provisioning depends on carrier (we'll include contingency in MAP)

3) Redwood ops (Irene/Karthik): finalize the attach runbook and provide a short ops briefing for Stonebridge SREs (30–45m).

Action items in MAP (attached): dates for PO, window for hardware delivery, Redwood onboarding prep, and a DocuSign link to the SOW. If these timelines look good we'll kick RFQs.
